callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# pr-1222: chore(pin): awf workflows track @main — always-latest policy (kicker fixes live on merge)

## Description

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Mitigation: awf main is load-bearing — review-gated pushes only; stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref); the agents submodule gitlink stays an immutable ENGINE pin via factory_ref.

Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

blocks.text:
factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## PR Description

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Mitigation: awf main is load-bearing — review-gated pushes only; stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref); the agents submodule gitlink stays an immutable ENGINE pin via factory_ref.

Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

**CRITICAL FINDING**: The PR description claims:

> "stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref)"

But the actual guard test `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` asserts the OPPOSITE — it asserts that refs are 40-hex immutable SHAs:
- `'ai-teammate.yml pins factory-teammate.yml at an immutable SHA'` — expects `RegExp(r'^[0-9a-f]{40}$')` to match.
- Same for machine-sm.yml and machine-merge.yml.

So after this PR changes `uses:` to `@main`, those tests will FAIL. `main` does not match `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`. This is a BLOCKING CI break — the PR does not update the guard tests.

Also the lockstep test compares refs of teammate/sm/merge — those would all be 'main' so the lockstep test would pass, but the three SHA tests would fail.

Additionally, `merge-trigger.yml` (factory-merge-trigger.yml) and `sm-kicker.yml` (factory-sm-kicker.yml) were changed to `@main` too, but they are NOT covered by the guard test at all (the guard test only covers the three stubs). The PR description says "stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main" — this is false on two counts: (1) the tests currently assert the opposite (immutable SHA), and (2) kicker/merge-trigger aren't in the stubs map.

    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # pr-1222: chore(pin): awf workflows track @main — always-latest policy (kicker fixes live on merge)

## Description

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Mitigation: awf main is load-bearing — review-gated pushes only; stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref); the agents submodule gitlink stays an immutable ENGINE pin via factory_ref.

Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

blocks.text:
factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

    with:

    secrets:

      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The `@main` flip itself matches the owner directive (the mutable-ref supply-chain trade-off is explicitly accepted; the `factory_ref` ENGINE pin correctly stays a SHA), but the PR ships with **red CI**: the guard test `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` still asserts immutable 40-hex SHAs and fails 3 tests against `@main` (verified locally), so the description's claimed mitigation — "guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main" — is inverted, not implemented.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — CI break: 3 guard tests fail (`ref "main" is not a 40-hex SHA`); the file runs in CI `test-core` shard 1 via `scripts/test_shards.json`, so the merge gate stays red.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — guard covers only teammate/SM/merge; the flipped `sm-kicker.yml` and `merge-trigger.yml` legs are unguarded, and `merge-trigger.yml`'s `secrets: inherit` is inconsistent with the explicit-mapping rule enforced on the other three.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — stale comments in `ai-teammate.yml` / `machine-sm.yml` still argue the immutable-SHA policy and cite the (now failing) guard directly above the new `@main` refs.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — no CHANGELOG entry for the policy switch (prior pin flips got one, e.g. #1146).

**Next Steps**:
1. Rewrite `factory_stub_ref_test.dart` to assert every awf `uses:` is exactly `@main` (rejecting stale SHAs and random refs) and update its header comment.
2. Extend the guard's `stubs` map to all five callers, settling the `secrets: inherit` case for `merge-trigger.yml`.
3. Refresh the pin comments in `ai-teammate.yml` and `machine-sm.yml` to state the always-`main` policy.
4. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

blocks.text:
**CRITICAL FINDING**: The PR description claims:

> "stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref)"

But the actual guard test `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` asserts the OPPOSITE — it asserts that refs are 40-hex immutable SHAs:
- `'ai-teammate.yml pins factory-teammate.yml at an immutable SHA'` — expects `RegExp(r'^[0-9a-f]{40}$')` to match.
- Same for machine-sm.yml and machine-merge.yml.

So after this PR changes `uses:` to `@main`, those tests will FAIL. `main` does not match `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`. This is a BLOCKING CI break — the PR does not update the guard tests.

Also the lockstep test compares refs of teammate/sm/merge — those would all be 'main' so the lockstep test would pass, but the three SHA tests would fail.

Additionally, `merge-trigger.yml` (factory-merge-trigger.yml) and `sm-kicker.yml` (factory-sm-kicker.yml) were changed to `@main` too, but they are NOT covered by the guard test at all (the guard test only covers the three stubs). The PR description says "stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main" — this is false on two counts: (1) the tests currently assert the opposite (immutable SHA), and (2) kicker/merge-trigger aren't in the stubs map.

Let me check whether the PR actually modified the test file. The diff shows only 5 files, all workflow YAMLs. No test file changes. So CI will be red if tests run in CI. Let me check the CI workflow to see if these tests run. Let me check ci.yml.

Also check AGENTS.md for guidance about pinning policy. The repo is huge (115KB AGENTS.md). Let me grep for relevant sections: "pin", "factory_stub_ref", "SHA".

Also let me verify the test actually fails by running it. Let me first check whether dart is available. Running the specific test file would confirm.

Also, check `.github/workflows/` — is there any other file referencing the pins, e.g., docs? factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # pr-1222: chore(pin): awf workflows track @main — always-latest policy (kicker fixes live on merge)

## Description

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Mitigation: awf main is load-bearing — review-gated pushes only; stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref); the agents submodule gitlink stays an immutable ENGINE pin via factory_ref.

Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

blocks.text:
factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
